newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler "concerned" about new air bag rules.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler "concerned" about new air bag rules.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said it supports the federal government's plan to reduce the explosive force of air bags, but is concerned that other proposed rules may undermine the public's confidence in the safety devices.

In addition to "de-powered" air bags, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Friday proposed new rules that would allow vehicle owners to disconnect their air bags and would require mandatory warning labels, "smart" air bag systems by the 1999 model year and optional air bag cutoff switches by 2000.

"While we need to carefully study all the details of NHTSA's proposed actions, we are concerned that two of these actions may undermine the public's confidence in air bags as effective supplemental safety systems," Chrysler said in a statement.

"Specifically, we are concerned that overemphasis of on-off switches and air bag deactivation may send the wrong message to the vast majority of Americans who benefit from proper seat belt use and air bags," the company added.
Chrysler said its engineering work to de-power air bags -- based on the NHTSA proposal that includes a sled test for unbelted occupants -- is well underway.

Chrysler said it can begin installing modified air bags by next fall. The company also supports NHTSA's call for more stringent warning labels and said it will soon begin notifying its owners on proper air bag safety.
"With the industry producing one million air bag-equipped vehicles every 30 days, time is of the essence," Chrysler said.

Ford Motor Co said in a separate statment that it will put put de-powered air bags into production as soon as possible and will maintain "determined research efforts" on smart air bags that can sense occupant weight and position and adjust inflation accordingly.

"Ford will work with NHTSA and others tirelessly to introduce effective, de-powered air bags into production as soon as possible," the company said. "We will also be talking to and working with our customers to help them better understand the air bag proposals and so that we understand their concerns and preferences on the immediate issues."
